values.title: Three disciplines, one team
values.intro: Most clients come to us for one of these and stay for the other two. The same people carry your project from the first workshop to the last line of code.

items.title: Brand identity
items.text: Strategy, naming, logotypes, type and colour, packaging, and guidelines that keep it all consistent long after we hand over.

items.title: Websites
items.text: Editorial sites and online shops designed and built in-house, fast on a phone and simple for your own team to update.

items.title: Campaigns
items.text: Launches, theatre seasons and appeals across posters, film, social and print, with one idea running through all of it.

values.title: How a project runs
values.intro: Every project follows the same shape, whether it is a label or a 200-page website. You meet everyone doing the work in the first week.

image.alt: Niamh Docherty interviewing a client team around a table covered in notes

steps.title: Listen
steps.text: Two weeks of interviews with your team, your customers and the people who chose someone else. We write it up as a two-page brief you sign off.

image.alt: Early poster and label sketches pinned to a cork wall

steps.title: Sketch
steps.text: Two or three routes shown as real things: a label, a homepage, a poster on a wall. Never a logo floating on white.

image.alt: Ama Owusu reviewing a website build on two monitors with a designer

steps.title: Build
steps.text: We develop one route into a complete system and make it, with a weekly call and a shared board you can check at any time.

image.alt: A printed brand guidelines book open next to a laptop showing the guidelines site

steps.title: Hand over
steps.text: Guidelines, source files and training for your team, then a check-in 90 days after launch to fix what real use reveals.

values.title: Who you will work with
values.intro: Every project is led by one of the founders and made by the people below, from the first workshop to launch.

people.name: Isla Rennie
people.bio: Ran the design team at a London publisher for nine years before starting the studio. Leads our identity work and reads every brief twice.

people.name: Tomasz Wrona
people.bio: Typographer from Kraków, in Glasgow since 2009. Draws the custom lettering in most of our identities and teaches type one evening a week.

people.name: Niamh Docherty
people.bio: A former arts journalist. Runs the listening stage of every project and writes the words that end up on the posters and the walls.

people.name: Ama Owusu
people.bio: Leads our team of four developers and has built every site we have launched since 2019. Still answers the support inbox herself.

people.name: Callum Baird
people.bio: Our packaging and print specialist. Spent much of 2025 at a label printer in Paisley getting the Ardlin bottles exactly right.

people.name: Rosa Lindqvist
people.bio: Keeps budgets, schedules and printers in line, and makes sure every client knows what happens next week.

values.title: Small on purpose
values.body:
We start eight to ten projects a year and turn down more than we take on. That is what lets a founder sit in every meeting, and it is why we have stayed at fourteen people.

  • A four-day week since 2022, with Fridays kept for our own projects
  • Every piece of work credited to the people who made it
  • One paid week a year for teaching, writing or speaking

values.title: Before you write
values.text: The questions we hear most in a first call. Anything else, ask Niamh directly.

items.question: Do you take part in free pitches?
items.answer: No. We do not make unpaid creative work to win a project. We are glad to share past work, meet your team and write a detailed proposal at no cost.

items.question: What is the smallest project you take on?
items.answer: Our projects usually start at £14,000. For smaller pieces of work, existing clients can book studio days at £950 a day.

items.question: How far ahead do you book?
items.answer: Usually six to ten weeks. If you have a fixed launch date, get in touch as early as you can.

items.question: Do you work with clients outside Scotland?
items.answer: About a third of our clients are in England, Ireland and Scandinavia. We travel for the first workshop and run the rest of the project remotely.

items.question: Who owns the work at the end?
items.answer: You do. On final payment you get full rights to the identity, the code and every source file. We only ask to show the work in our portfolio.
